headline: French school protests spread across the country as pupils vow to keep going
deck: There have been nearly 2,000 arrests; 564 upper-secondary schools are affected.
standard: Pupils in France say they will keep protesting after Edouard Geffrey, the education minister, met their organisations on Friday.

The protests began on 21 September in deprived suburbs around Paris and have spread across the country. There have been nearly 2,000 arrests, and 564 of the country's 3,700 upper-secondary schools are affected. On Friday the authorities closed 400 of them and banned demonstrations.

Geffrey has withdrawn a proposal for higher fees at some institutions of higher education, which helped set off the unrest. The pupils' demands centre on absent teachers who are not replaced, crumbling buildings and classes of up to 36.
short: Pupils in France say they will keep protesting after meeting Edouard Geffrey, the education minister, on Friday. The protests began in the suburbs of Paris on 21 September and have spread across the country, with nearly 2,000 arrests and 564 upper-secondary schools affected.
